# hush_cloudinary_access_credential (Resource)

Manage Cloudinary access credentials in the Hush Security platform. With an Enterprise account management key, the access manager creates a product environment API key per policy version, gives it the privilege's role, and hands the workload `cloud_name`, `api_key`, `api_secret` and `cloudinary_url`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Create a Cloudinary dynamic access credential
resource "hush_cloudinary_access_credential" "example" {
  name           = "prod-cloudinary"
  description    = "Production Cloudinary credential"
  deployment_ids = [hush_deployment.example.id]
  account_id     = "abcde1fg-2345-6789-0abc-d1efg2hi3jkl"

  api_key_wo            = var.cloudinary_account_management_key
  api_key_wo_version    = "1"
  api_secret_wo         = var.cloudinary_account_management_secret
  api_secret_wo_version = "1"
}
```

## Requirements

**hush-am chart 0.34.2 or later** on the target deployment. On an older one
the apply fails.

**A Cloudinary Enterprise account.** The access manager uses the Provisioning
API, which Cloudinary enables on request, and the Permissions API. Both are
Enterprise only.

**An account management key.** Create one under **Settings > Account
Management Keys** in the Cloudinary Console; the page also shows the account
ID. In the product environments the privileges name, the key must be allowed
to create and delete API keys and to create, assign and delete roles; a key
with the Account Master Admin role is. It can only give a workload's key a
role whose permissions it holds itself; Cloudinary refuses any other with 403.
It reaches every product environment of the account, so treat it like an
admin key.

**Network egress** from the access manager to `api.cloudinary.com` on 443.

## Delivering the credentials

The access manager generates `cloud_name`, `api_key`, `api_secret` and
`cloudinary_url` for each policy version; `account_id` and the account
management key never reach a workload. By default an access policy delivers
`cloudinary_url` as `CLOUDINARY_URL`, which Cloudinary's SDKs read cloud name,
key and secret from.

## Changing `account_id`

A new account needs a new `api_key` and a new `api_secret` in the same apply,
which the plan checks, since an account management key works only in its own
account. The API refuses the change while an access policy or a dynamic
credential uses the credential, since Hush deletes keys and roles with the
newest root, which cannot reach the old account. The state keeps the old
account, key and secret, so the same configuration applies once nothing uses
the credential. To move to another account, create a credential for it.

## Changing the key or the secret

Every key or secret sent issues new credentials to every policy that uses the
credential, so the provider sends each only when `api_key` (`api_secret`) or
`api_key_wo_version` (`api_secret_wo_version`) changes. Moving from `api_key`
to `api_key_wo` sends it too, even when the value is the same.

If the apply fails while Hush syncs the new key or secret, the state keeps it,
since Hush already holds it. A credential left in error takes a new key or
secret, or a bumped version.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account_id` (String) The Cloudinary account ID, as **Settings > Account Management Keys** shows it: 1 to 128 letters, digits, '_' or '-'. Changing it requires a new `api_key` and a new `api_secret` (or bumped `api_key_wo_version` and `api_secret_wo_version`)
- `deployment_ids` (List of String) List of deployment IDs that can access this credential. Currently limited to a single deployment. Changing this after creation is not supported; the credential must be deleted and recreated.
- `name` (String) The name of the Cloudinary access credential

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) The account management key: the key of an Enterprise account's **Settings > Account Management Keys** pair. The access manager creates and deletes the workloads' product environment keys and their roles with it; it never reaches a workload. Every change issues new credentials to every policy that uses the credential
- `api_key_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The account management key (write-only). More secure than `api_key` because Terraform will not store this value in the state file.
- `api_key_wo_version` (String) Used to trigger updates for `api_key_wo`. Change when the key changes.
- `api_secret` (String, Sensitive) The secret of the account management key. Every change issues new credentials to every policy that uses the credential
- `api_secret_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The secret of the account management key (write-only). More secure than `api_secret` because Terraform will not store this value in the state file.
- `api_secret_wo_version` (String) Used to trigger updates for `api_secret_wo`. Change when the secret changes.
- `description` (String) The description of the Cloudinary access credential
- `secret_store_id` (String) The ID of the secret store where this credential is saved (optional)

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the Cloudinary access credential
- `kind` (String) The kind of access credential
- `type` (String) The type of access credential
